[USER] The user is planning out their garden layout.  
[USER] The user attended a local gardening workshop at the community center.  
[USER] The user learned about companion planting and natural pest control at the workshop.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Companion planting is a way to create a harmonious and balanced ecosystem in the garden.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Tomatoes benefit from companion planting with basil, marigold, borage, chives, oregano, and comfrey.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Basil repels pests like whiteflies and aphids and adds flavor to tomato dishes.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Marigold repels nematodes and attracts beneficial insects like ladybugs and lacewings.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Borage attracts beneficial insects and improves tomato flavor and texture.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Chives repel aphids and add nutrients to the soil.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Oregano is a natural fungicide that helps prevent diseases in tomatoes.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Comfrey acts as a fertilizer plant and brings up nutrients from the subsoil.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Avoid planting tomatoes near fennel, kohlrabi, and members of the Brassica family (broccoli, cauliflower, cabbage).  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Additional tips include planting tomatoes with flowers like nasturtiums, calendula, and sunflowers, and incorporating herbs like parsley, dill, and cilantro.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The "Three Sisters" approach involves planting tomatoes with corn and beans for mutual benefits.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Companion planting is not a substitute for good gardening practices like crop rotation and pest management.  
[USER] The user is particularly interested in trying out the "Three Sisters" method.  
[USER] The user is seeking advice on how to space corn, beans, and tomatoes properly.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Corn should be planted in the center of the bed, in blocks or hills, with 3-4 plants per hill, spaced 3-4 feet apart.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Beans should be planted around the base of the corn, about 3-4 inches away, spaced 2-3 inches apart.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Tomatoes should be planted around the perimeter of the bed, about 2-3 feet away from corn and beans, spaced 2-3 feet apart.
